We evaluate the precision of the current measurement of the $B^0_s\rightarrow K^+K^-$ lifetime ratio, denoted as $\tau_{bs}/\tau_b$. The analysis relies on data from the LHCb and ALICE collaborations, which contribute with independent datasets, resulting in a current precision of approximately 1%. The analysis also involves theoretical inputs to assess the accuracy of the present experimental assessment.

This study stands out as an examination of a random sine-Gordon equation, which has a discrete spatial structure and an unbounded domain for time. The discrete control problem is formulated to minimize the difference between a solution component and a desired function, along with associated costs of control efforts. The definition of a feasible control involves the use of approximating operators to demonstrate that a optimal control exists. The document provides the characteristics of the optimal control, as well as a solution to a related quasi-varational problem. Finally, the paper shows that as the discretization interval approaches zero, a set of densely compacted values can be identified that converges to a compact value, which is a solution to a specific time-dependent Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation. The solution to this time-dependent Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation also characterizes the optimal value function of the given control problem.

Our analysis of highly energetic surface-detected events reveals significant anisotropies in an energetic map created by converting event energies into anisotropic tensor components. By focusing on anisotropic coefficients, we identify an excess of events moving towards the southern celestial pole in an energetic map of trigalactic coordinates above 4 EeV. These directions of motion correlate with previously identified low-energy CR anisotropies and are aligned with the plane of the Milky Way. Additionally, we calculate dipolar anisotropy amplitudes from 4-8 EeV to 31.8 EeV to be between 4.4% and 7.7%, these values coincide with the end of the vertical spread of the low-energy CR spectrum. Furthermore, anisotropy amplitules at 107.8 EeV and above are estimated to be 7.3% and above, based on anisotropy multipolar components less than 15.8 EeV which account for 41% of anisotropy description power.

The ATLAS detector at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) is capable of measuring charged particles with high accuracy, utilizing its inner tracking system which comprises layers of silicon detectors and a calorimeter. These measurements can provide valuable data for studying the content and alteration of nuclei caused by the interaction of protons with heavy ions, specifically in the context of p+Pb and Pb+Pb collisions. By comparing the nuclear alteration factors (RAF) of various particle types including photons, charged particles, and neutral hadrons, researchers can better understand this interaction. To achieve this, they have collected data from p+Pb and Pb+Pb collisions at a specific center-of-mass energy and analyzed the distribution of particles in transverse momentum. Additionally, they have extended their analysis to include data from proton-proton collisions at a similar energy level and present these findings with associated uncertainties.

Various types of noncommutative probability spaces can be linked to specific Lie groups or their associated Lie algebras, allowing us to investigate how these spaces evolve over time through the examination of corresponding differential equations within those algebras. This connection enables us to derive useful insights, such as identifying moments and generating series for a broad class of dynamical systems, and can be applied to resolve previously challenging problems, including a long-standing issue with the Phosphorus-32 decay pattern.

Our research focuses on developing a sophisticated method to categorize small cells within tumor images, specifically using data from pathologist-stained images. By analyzing these images, we aim to provide support for pathologists in interpreting complex images and extracting relevant features. Although standard techniques have been successful in identifying entire tumor images, categorizing these images by counting small cells within them is a more intricate task due to the need to recognize numerous closely-spaced cells with varying characteristics. As the number of distinct types of cells increases, it becomes necessary to process a vast amount of data. To address this challenge of working with limited data, we explored a technique known as federated learning, which enables the training of models across multiple independent datasets without the need to share or centralize the data. Through the application of federated learning, we were able to develop a high-performing model that excelled in accurately identifying and categorizing cells within images, outperforming conventional techniques using a single centralized database.

Decision-feedback equalizers are crucial for reducing the need for equalization in the equalizer, making them popular in high-speed underwater optical communication systems. However, their effectiveness is limited due to residual chromatic dispersion that varies with wavelength, which severely impacts system performance when using coarse optical filters necessary for increasing system robustness against transmission losses. This issue is particularly pronounced when it comes to mitigating large transmission losses in undersea links, where new equalization techniques are needed to combat the associated peak distortion and the resulting burst errors that conventional forward-error correction methods struggle to handle. In this paper, a novel equalization system is proposed to minimize transmission losses in underwater optical communication systems by a unique equalization technique and an optimized filter design. This decision-feedback equalization system is demonstrated to reduce the need for equalization by up to 14.49 ns in a high-speed (50 Gb/s) undersea transmission experiment, significantly improving system robustness against large transmission losses in the 125-km to 250-km range in the blue window (450 nm). Additionally, the proposed equalization system is found to reduce the bit-error-rate by up to four orders of magnitude in a 250-km link experiment.

Deep Learning frameworks like Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCNs) have achieved significant success in handling time-series data. TCNs employ dilated convolutions to efficiently capture temporal dependencies at various scales. TCNs can be customized with different filter sizes and dilation factors, but determining the optimal configuration for a specific task remains a complex challenge due to the vast design space and lack of straightforward evaluation methods. To address this challenge, we introduce a novel network structure optimizer called Trimming In Time, which leverages TCNs and an auxiliary network to find a suitable architecture that balances accuracy and computational efficiency. We evaluate Trimming In Time's performance across multiple datasets and tasks, and its results show that the optimal configuration it identifies consistently outperforms existing alternatives while requiring comparable computational resources.

It has been proven that all Zinbiel algebras possess a specific characteristic - they are solvable, meaning that each of its Lie adjoint representations is solvable. This implication leads to the conclusion that Zinbiel upper derivations are necessarily finite. Furthermore, a specific set of rules has been established to facilitate the conversion of a nonassociative algebra into a Zinbiel algebra, and the corresponding algebras that 'precede' these rules have been classified for two-dimensional representations. Notably, for any such representation, the corresponding Lie adjoint modules are irreducible, and the alisors of any such Zinbiel algebra are isomorphic to the algebra itself.

Our analysis explores flow coefficient differences among various particle types (ppc) in Pb-Pb collisions, specifically focusing on how they vary with transverse momentum ($p_{\rm T}$) and centrality for collisions at a high energy level of $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}$ = 5.02 TeV. By combining results from previous studies and our findings, we differentiate between initial conditions influencing collisions and how particles move after the fact. Additionally, we investigate the relationship between flow coefficient differences and the number of participating particles, as well as examine ppc for different types of particles with respect to their phase-space position.

The concept of fuzzy logic has been generalized to encompass a broader scope, specifically through the use of lattice-valued logics, and this generalization has been explored through the use of DLE-logics. As a result of this framework, we have been able to derive a unified inverse implication operator that is compatible with a specific set of properties, including the residual property, within the DLE-logic setting. The developed properties of this inverse operator enable it to serve as a foundation for defining a range of connections between logical constructs, including those found in Kleene star semantics, and this framework has been applied to derive solutions to various equation types within the DLE-logic setting. The solutions to these equations can then be utilized to establish the validity of inequalities in the direction of inequality, including those found in the Solvability of Inequalities in the Direction of Inequality (SII) and the Strengthened Inequalities in the Direction of Inequality (SII) theorems, and through the introduction of a new construct, the strong DLE-logic, we have been able to establish the validity of the sSIP and apply it to a range of equation and inequality types, including those found in the Strong Scheduling Theory (SST) and the Strong Inequalities in the Direction of Inequality (SII) settings, and through the use of the strong DLE-logic, we have been able to establish the validity of the sSIP and apply

In maintaining table consistency across different datasets, functional dependencies are crucial constraints to consider. These dependencies govern the connection between rows and are essential for linking related data. However, their definition becomes complicated when missing values, or nulls, are involved. Previous attempts to manage this issue have primarily relied on interpreting nulls as unknown potential values. This approach often leads to significant issues, such as treating unrelated datasets as inherently linked simply because they both contain a specific undefined value. This problem is particularly prominent in scenarios involving outer joins, which are frequently used to combine seemingly unrelated tables. This research is centered on addressing these issues with a focus on handling tables with nulls in line with a common industry standard. This line of investigation is particularly relevant for data quality control, constraint propagation, and data integration systems.

Existing tools for analyzing time series with count data are limited, particularly in handling seasonal patterns. To address this, we created an innovative model that accounts for temporal variations and seasonality in multiple streams of non-negative time series data. Our unique formulation allows for a flexible approach to seasonality, with each component capable of following distinct parametric distributions. To estimate model parameters, we utilized an efficient iterative method for obtaining a maximum likelihood estimate. Demonstrating the effectiveness of our model, we conducted simulations and applied it to forecast monthly subway ridership.

This paper introduces the concept of Neural Description Fields (NDFs) as a novel object representation, designed to efficiently capture complex objects with high point cloud complexity. NDFs utilize a set of sinusoidal functions that equivariantly describe object surfaces in response to transformations in three-dimensional space. By employing an Equivariant Point Network (EPN), which utilizes Cross Attention Layers (CALs) and SE(3)-Transformation Networks (STNs), object features and descriptors are extracted and transformed, respectively. The result is a precise and robust object classifier, achieved through a combination of Random Forest (RF) and Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) networks. Experimental data indicates that NDFs outperform existing methods in both classification accuracy and runtime performance. Additionally, an extension of the NDF framework is proposed, which enables joint object manipulation and scene reconstruction, demonstrating the framework's versatility in handling diverse applications.

The SiD Detracker design is a highly effective inner tracking system with excellent point-reconstruction capabilities, yet its heavy mass and associated physical challenges led to an initiative within the CMS collaboration to modify the SiD detector's trajectory reconstruction performance. This could enable the SiD detector to meet the baseline criteria while reducing its mass and associated challenges.

This study examines the properties of a dense star cluster in the Galactic bulge, identified as Tonantzintla 2. We discovered that this cluster, which contains approximately 3,000 solar masses and 90,000 years old, has a compact core with a radius of 1.39 parsecs. By analyzing the cluster's colors and velocities across its surface, we found no evidence of variations related to age, metal content, or motion. This indicates that Tonantzintla 2 is a well-mixed cluster, capable of retaining its contents due to its dense structure. We predict that further observations in the future may reveal smaller substructures within the cluster.

The proliferation of verified code, formally proven theorems, and executable definitions within the Isabelle Archive of Formal Proofs makes it an ideal framework for exploring computer-aided reasoning. To facilitate further research and expose promising directions for investigation, a carefully curated framework is required to provide consistent, transparent, and modularly accessible analyses via the AFP. This requirement has led to the introduction of a new, adaptable framework in the Isabelle Isabelle AFP, which includes a set of design principles, methods, and tools to streamline the development of research within specific domains or on isolated problems, as exemplified in the works on inductively defined relations, probabilistic reasoning, and modular reasoning, as well as on theorem proofs in algebraic structures, as detailed in the associated formalizations.

This study seeks to identify the position of the Yang-Lee edge singularity within the standard grid of O(N) universality classes by examining the critical behavior of the Yang-Lee edge in various traditional, non-chiral, order-parameter symmetries near a second-order phase transition point in d=2. Using high-precision numerical methods, specifically Monte Carlo simulations with system sizes up to L=26, we determine the standard and anomalous critical exponents associated with the Yang-Lee edge, which are then used to elucidate its critical behavior in relation to known O(N) universality classes. Our analysis reveals that, for model A, the standard critical exponent θ matches that of the critical dimension of the same traditional O(N) universality class where the Yang-Lee edge singularity aligns with a known, non-marginal positive value. For cases θ that correspond to known, non-marginal positive values, we establish that θ is equal to the sum of the standard critical exponent φ and the anomalous component, i.e., θ = φ + i. Ultimately, this research provides a framework for understanding the position of the Yang-Lee edge singularity within the standard grid of O(N) universality classes, which may also provide insight into resolving the long-standing controversy regarding the nature of the Lee-Yang edge in the Ising model.

In statistics and machine learning, it is frequently essential to establish whether an optimization algorithm is minimizing a convex function. Within the context of approximate message passing (AMP), our research offers two significant advancements: Firstly, we have developed a general mechanism to ascertain the convergence of the AMP iterates to a local minimum, which exhibits scalability relative to system size. This implies that for problems like sparse PCA, Sudakov-Fernique's inequality ensures the local minimality of the converged solution. Moreover, our improved understanding of the convergence behavior enables an enhancement to prior results concerning Sudakov-Fernique's application in estimating the free energy landscape, as seen in the paper by Mitterjäger and Montanari. Secondly, we have provided an alternative, universally applicable method to demonstrate the local convexity of the TAP free energy landscape, which is relevant to the analysis of the AMP landscape. This method relies on establishing the non-negative definiteness of the Hessian matrix of the posterior distribution.

Modern metasurfaces, which are engineered surfaces composed of minute unit structures,  
offer exceptional control over light and other electromagnetic waves. Due to their vast  
potential, investigating these cutting-edge technologies requires simulating interactions  
with waves using computational methods. This paper outlines key approaches to  
metasurface examination in Computational Electromagnetics, focusing on efficient  
models for periodic structures. By leveraging these models, we can leverage large-scale  
parallel processing to conduct simulations of intricate interactions between lasers, radio waves, and periodic metasurfaces.

This research paper addresses the local orbital linearization problem for smooth, totally integrable vector fields in Euclidean space. Key internal invariants are identified to facilitate local orbital linearization of these vector fields. Specific conditions have been derived to determine when these invariants are non-singular, thereby establishing the orbitally linearizable nature of the given totally integrable vector field.

This investigation focuses on generating comprehensive CI electron correlations in quantum systems. To do this, we transform the difficult many-body Schrödinger equation into a binary classification problem. We then design and train a binary classifier that accurately predicts the energy of configurations, effectively capturing the correlation effects. Notably, our method requires and leverages a vast amount of training data, which can be obtained from low-quality initial configurations. As a result, our neural network learns to predict the exact CI energies for various molecular molecules, including H2, He, and Li2. These examples demonstrate that our deep learning approach can be used to capture the full spectrum of electron correlation in multiple atomic/molecular systems.

The discovery of the massive, U-shaped galaxy group G21-4-1, spanning over a million light-years near the Milky Way's galactic center, is described in this research. Using data from the Milky Way's radio map, specifically 408 MHz, we identified this extraordinary structure for the first time. Further investigation with the Planck's galaxy map revealed that G21-4-1 also emits in the frequency of 35.2 GHz. However, it doesn't emit visible light. We believe that G21-4-1 is not collections of individual objects but rather ionized hydrogen gas and galaxies caught in the process of being accreted into the Milky Way. Its detection is significant as it highlights that small, scattered galaxy structures can have a noticeable impact on the galaxy's evolution.

Precise understanding of how aerosols affect the Earth's energy system is crucial for improving climate change predictions. While the current ability to assess aerosol properties from space is limited, particularly due to the lack of night-time satellite observations, researchers are now utilizing night-time stellar photometry to tackle this issue. By analyzing the light from background stars that has been altered by the Earth's atmosphere, this technique allows for night-only mapping of aerosols. While the ability to assess aerosol properties from the aerosol-to-Rayleigh signal is currently limited due to noise, a new approach has been demonstrated using the Mauna Kea data, which utilizes the atmospheric signal and successfully reduces the error rates for key aerosol properties by up to a tenfold increase, bringing them within reasonable ranges for atmospheric research. By leveraging the rich dataset from global photometric surveys, this research may lead to more precise assessments of how aerosols affect the Earth's energy system from space.

This research paper introduces DeepHMap++, an innovative neural network architecture for precise pose estimation in a wide range of angles (from -90 to 90 degrees) using only depth information from 3D sensing technologies like Time-of-Flight or structured light. The base architecture, DeepHMap, utilized a two-stage process involving clustering and response learning to pose estimation but struggled with accuracy at extreme angles. We propose the DeepHMap++ model, which employs a merged strategy combining full-dimensional projection and clustering techniques, enhanced by correspondence learning in a single, highly parameterized layer. The results of our experiments and comparisons with DeepHMap and other state-of-the-art methods demonstrate the superiority of our approach in achieving high accuracy across a wide spectrum of pose estimation angles.

Nonlocal theories are gaining significant attention in scientific communities due to their ability to model and predict the rate-dependent fracture and damage evolution in complex materials, including the interaction between fractures and fluids. These theories focus on a nonlocal influence of the degraded material's microstructure on its surrounding environment, where the term "nonlocal" refers to the consideration of an extended neighborhood in space, as the theories are spatially local. This review introduces bond-oriented peridynamics, a type of nonlocal mechanical theory, and explores its parallels with other nonlocal theories, while also highlighting their commonalities and differences, as well as their shared objectives and purposes. Given their recent success in predicting the mentioned complex dynamics and the potential for 99% of these theories to be reclassified under the bond-oriented peridynamics framework, this review focuses on bond-oriented peridynamics and presents new proposals for developing bond-oriented peridynamic models that incorporate the interaction between fluid flow and complex dynamics.

We present the Generalized Graphical Lasso (GGLasso) library, written in Python, for addressing the Generalized Graphical Lasso problem. This challenge arises when recovering a positive-definite matrix from corrupted, non-gaussian data, and is commonly applied in Brain-Computer Interface systems and other fields. Unlike the standard Graphical Lasso problem with a multivariate normal distribution, the Generalized variant has no restrictive assumptions, making it suitable for a wider range of applications. Due to its complexity, specialized algorithms are necessary to find the solution. We detail the GGLasso library, which implements a recent, efficient method for solving this difficult problem, providing users with a reliable tool to achieve high accuracy results.

Numerous simulation techniques are utilized to sample configurations of molecules or material systems according to their statistical weight, with one approach being solving the Laplace equation for molecular inversely weighted configurations, where the weight is determined by the systems' energy. However, some systems, characterized by substantial molecular interactions, flexible structures, or complex geometries, contain numerous deep local minima that hinder standard simulation methods, even those incorporating geometric constraints or stochastic geometry integrators, which can trap systems in these minima and produce inaccurate results. This study proposes the use of modified Langevin dynamics, featuring a geometric integrator, for exploring the configurational space of these challenging molecular systems, allowing controlled temperature exploration to determine temperature ranges for reliable sampling, as illustrated by comparisons of water dimer-trimer energy distributions, decane, and glycerol densities to simulated and experimental data, respectively, showing favorable results, with further findings reported in supplementary materials about system robustness, convergence, and efficiency.

This research builds a new class of simulations that model the accretion of matter around merging black holes from the remnant's wave shadow. Our primary simulations are based on viscous scalar dark matter that does not interact through forces, although the framework can be adapted for other types of dark matter. We've also applied a radiative transfer method to produce the images seen in black holes. These simulations are crucial for distinguishing between various models of dark matter, particularly those involving low-mass particles. We've observed that the size of the accretion disk's peak depends heavily on the mass of the dark matter. We've also found that, under certain conditions, the amount of dark matter that falls into the newly formed black hole is so minimal that it behaves much like a traditional general relativity scenario. However, in other cases, the dark matter significantly alters the appearance of the accretion disk, making it appear larger, smaller, or both, depending on the specific model.

We investigate the long-term behavior of a specific type of beam, named the extended Euler-Bernoulli beam, which is situated on a special type of network that resembles a star. This investigation involves studying how certain external forces affect the beam's overall stability. It has been demonstrated that a discrete control method can effectively stabilize various forms of damping, ensuring that external forces decrease at a rate of $O(1/\sqrt{t})$ as time progresses. Furthermore, the presence of equivalent external forces can significantly impact the long-term behavior of the system. Notably, the systems exhibit complete descent properties, meaning that the external forces eventually disappear at a rate of $O(1/t)\log\left(2+C/t\right)$ as time increases, which illustrates a clear connection between continuous and discrete dissipation mechanisms.

Researchers have developed a novel material with exceptional acoustic and transparent properties, enabling acoustic lenses with increased transmission and transverse range. These transformers transform small transducers into large-array equivalents, thus detecting acoustic waves from wider angles and improving data collection efficiency and spatial resolution. A prototype of this material was tested frequency-range (5-50 MHz) against established alternatives and demonstrated minimal energy loss, excellent transmission when combined with conventional transducers, and enhanced detection capabilities. Findings reveal significantly improved data collection efficiency, spatial resolution, and beam penetration depth, with implications for high-performance extensive detectors in advanced photoacoustic breast imaging systems.

Community detection is viewed as identifying the most prominent groups within a network. This concept, which applies to single networks, extends to multilayer networks that consist of multiple interconnected networks. To find the most significant community within multilayer networks, we've developed the between-prominence vector, which identifies the largest prominence vector across the individual networks that make up the multilayer network. By equating between-prominence values, we can identify distinct communities in multilayer networks. Our approach was tested on artificial and real-world data, and it outperformed existing methods, including the Multilayer Blockmodel Method, in accuracy and runtime efficiency. Notably, the between-prominence vector method requires no initial parameters and produces concise, high-quality community detections.

Current single-task models struggle to handle the multiple degradations that occur when capturing digital images, which include demosaicing, denoising and deblurring. In contrast, utilizing the Bayer raw image as the input image allows a collaborative approach where these three tasks can be completed by a unified, deep Bayesian deconvolution (UDBA) model. By training this model using variational message passing, we found that it establishes non-reciprocal degradation sequences and enables each task to benefit from the others. By replacing the VMP training with circular adversarial training, we developed a Unified Collaborative Deblurring, Demosaicing and Denising (UCDD) model, which leads to significant performance improvements when compared to separate models for each task and pre-trained models, particularly in the deblurring step.

This study delves into the properties of a quantum field that follows from a non-relativistic spacetime, which can be described using a parameter $R$ that modifies its structure. By examining the spacetime through various approaches - including geometric, algebraic, and quantum mechanical methods - we derive the geometric properties of a field with $s$-fold symmetry and analyze its behavior in both standard Minkowski spacetime (where $R$ equals its relativistic value) and a novel spacetime (where $R$ is non-relativistic). We establish the sufficient conditions for the existence of massless modes in spacetimes, and find that Minkowski spacetime supports only fields that are related to particles with finite spins, whereas the new spacetime allows for a wider range of behaviors, and we, and derive the form of the Dirac equation in this new spacetime, and investigate the characteristics of its solutions, and establish its connection to the well-known results for the standard Dirac particle.

This project introduces an advanced causal exploration framework, building upon the 'causal-learn' library, which allows for the inference of high-level causality structures from data. Using the 'Parent-child' algorithm, this framework can generate a causal network by identifying direct influences, and it is particularly useful in various applications such as identifying key feature relationships in data sets. Developed in Python 3 using the 'NetworkX' and 'NetworkXLayout' packages, this framework is an open-source initiative available on GitHub.

A study on how spheres interact with liquid surfaces entry-related to their velocity was conducted in an intermediate speed range, and to support this research, a new, automated high-speed imaging system was created, allowing for frame-by-frame visualization of the sphere's entry process. By utilizing this system, the surface seal thickness as it forms was measured and compared to theoretical models, and the results showed that existing equations either did not apply to this intermediate speed range or required modification. A new formula was then proposed and could accurately describe the surface seal thickness for the sphere at these moderate speed regimes.

In a well-studied category of Type IIB string theory effective theories that include supergravity, we've identified an atypical set of theories capable of exhibiting non-trivial, non-Abelian, chiral, and mixed anomalies within their zero-energy configuration space. This capability is unique because most models are limited to exhibiting only non-Abelian flat-space symmetries in their vacuum states. The models in question, however, exhibit a striking contrast by exhibiting breaking of conformal, chiral, and diffeomorphism symmetries, despite being derived from Type IIB supergravity which initially possesses a high degree of symmetry. The models in question also demonstrate the unexpected occurrence of extended, topological terms that are tied to the charges of gravitational instantons. These terms arise in models where quantum field theoretical consistency is quite different from previous models. Specifically, the models require the inclusion of charged magnetic monopoles in order to account for the terms associated with gravitational instantons. As a technical development, we've derived a set of general conditions that would enable the emergence of such terms in models of this kind.

Recent studies suggest incorporating memory security modules (MSMs) into a main system could enhance security systems like secure enclave, though it introduced a new concern - "confidence". Although MSM provides reliability in security algorithms, users may still doubt the authenticity of a system's content due to the potential for undetected malicious modifications. We investigate methods to minimize the necessary physical isolation size in order to achieve low confidence requirements. We developed an optimization model to determine the most effective physically-isolated components, thus reducing the necessary size. Based on a user study, we formed several designs with the smallest physical isolation, discovering that displaying an watermark or an icon in the corner of the main screen is particularly convincing. We verified these prototypes with actual security modules, and found that the most convincing design required only 1/9th of the computing resources used in previous approaches.

Deep learning methods have gained significant popularity due to their versatility, 
however, their reliable operation has been a challenge to overcome. 
Research has been conducted to address these issues, 
yet existing solutions have struggled to withstand minor and uncommon events, 
and their vulnerabilities to large-scale disruptions remain unaddressed. 
In this research, we introduce a new problem setting that captures scenarios 
of sudden, severe information loss encountered by policies during real-world deployments. 
We formulate the problem of gradient optimization with partially missing observations 
and introduce a new approach called Resilient Policy Gradient (PRPG). 
Notably, our PRPG involves a innovative transformation of gradient calculations 
which enables the compensation for severely degraded observations. 
Our PRPG ensures the compensation of severely degraded observations 
by equating them to their corresponding, complete counterparts. 
Our findings demonstrate the superiority of Resilient Policy Gradient (PRPG) 
over previously established methods through enhanced compensation of severely degraded information. 
The effectiveness of PRPG is further evidenced by its superior performance 
in tasks of conversation, driving, diagnosis, and text translation.

In the context of the box game, we consider an n-point selection list where players make choices, but a critical issue arises when players are restricted to selecting only a few options due to memory, cognitive limitations, or the high cost of picking multiple options. We find that this limitation causes players to concentrate on the highest-paying options, which in turn causes a significant drop in options diversity. Contrary to standard economic theory, we observe that offering players multiple selections always leads to less diversity. Experimental data supports this finding and further reveals that options diversity can actually increase as the number of selections decreases. Given these observations, we conclude that providing consumers with multiple choices isn't always beneficial for diversity, and thus, regulatory measures should take this fact into consideration.

Cubanite, a paramagnetic sulfide, exhibits structural characteristics similar to a ferromagnetic Lirotenite, resulting in the latter's orbital-selective behavior. Through experimental measurements of magnetic susceptibility and x-ray photoemission spectroscopy, along with theoretical calculations of x-ray spectra, we discovered that orbital-selective occupancy also occurs in the semimetallic Cubanite. In contrast to ferromagnetic Lirotenite, the orbital-selective behavior in antiferromagnetic Cubanite manifests at the opposite Fermi level.

A remarkable phenomenon occurs in our study as the massive, dark excitons in a twisted $B i_2 I_3$ $T M D I_2$ show large-scale coherent size oscillations without the need for an external magnetic field. The unique properties of the $T M D I_2$ include exceptionally low dark exciton mass and a substantial valley decoherence time. These characteristics enable the creation of dark excitons with a mass near zero, facilitated by the $K$-point $E G$ gap of $B i_2 I_3$ and a strong valley coupling induced by the $T M D I_2$ layer, resulting in a substantial Rabi frequency while maintaining a long lifetime. This makes $T M D I_2$ an outstanding candidate for practical applications involving the manipulation of light-like quasiparticles in the realm of quantum technologies.

In two-dimensional non-symmorphic lattices, lattice symmetry mandates the existence of Dirac points within electronic or photonic lattice models. We investigate the unique properties offered by non-symmorphic lattices, focusing on their ability to host Dirac points, in the context of a lattice derived from non-interlocking X-shaped monomers. A 2D lattice model is examined that offers significant advantages, allowing for precise identification of Dirac points' positions, as well as potential topological properties, including Chern numbers and valley Hall effects. Extending this research to include spin-orbit coupling yields additional effects, such as the spin-valley Hall effect, within both lattice and moire superlattices. We observe that the uniqueness of non-symmorphic symmetry ensures the stability of topological features, while the degree of symmetry provides control, and the potential for gapless moire valleys to facilitate spin-valley locked current, within these advanced 2D structures.

Quantum states exhibiting properties beyond those allowed by local realism are called squeezed states, serving as the foundation for next-generation quantum technologies. Lacking, however, are schemes capable of efficiently generating highly non-classical continuous-variable states, essential for processing information carried by optical modes, based on discrete variables. This research investigates a specific type of non-classical light, known as single-photon facilitated coherent states, created through an optical process called quantum-optical catalysis, featuring strong non-linear correlations attributable to the presence of a single photon. We demonstrate that these states exhibit significant squeezed-displaced non-separability, making them suitable for the secure transmission of information carried by multiple photons, resulting in a level of secrecy closer to that of quantum key distribution, even in the presence of an active eavesdropper. Furthermore, we find that single-photon facilitated coherent states can also serve as sensitive indicators of interactions between light and matter, allowing for measurements of extremely weak non-linear processes, such as two-photon down-conversion, not directly accessible with standard coherent states.

This research employs the Newman-Penrose formalism to analyze the Lagrangian of charged test particles moving in curved spacetime, written in the first-order Hamilton-Jacobi form. By utilizing the Weitzenb\'{a}ck formula, we transform the Lagrangian into a form where the coupling of a charged particle's bivector, the electromagnetic 2-form, and the Chern-Weil term involving the Riemann curvature's Weyl component are made apparent. In the specific framework of first-order Palatini variation, our approach reveals how a charged particle's bivector couples with the Weyl curvature metric. Furthermore, we demonstrate using Newman-Penrose coefficients how a constant electromagnetic field in flat spacetime, resulting in a linear Weyl tensor, leads to resonant RP effects in a manner compatible with Dirac's large numbers hypothesis. Our findings are further verified through an example of resonant gravitational ray optics in flat spacetime, as described by Newman-Penrose coefficients.

Predicting polymer properties based on blending base materials is the primary focus of this research. We examine the potential of using a linear regression model in conjunction with SMT solvers to solve the algebraic equations that arise when combining ingredients. Our approach involves applying the regression model to four existing polymer datasets, utilizing features derived from the原材料 properties. We observe improved results by incorporating additional binary decision variables, which either include or exclude base materials in the final product. This method can be adapted to fulfill specific product requirements, such as ensuring the inclusion of certain base materials.

Music production professionals are constantly seeking innovative methods to enrich the soundscape of tracks, particularly those emulating organic instruments. Human vocalizations, for instance, contain rich harmonic content that audio producers canemerge two individuals breathing into a microphone and utilize a transcription model to separate the sounds into distinct signals. These separated sounds canthen be applied various creative enhancement techniques, such as adjusting volume, adding reverb, or even substituting with full organic instrument recordings. To demonstrate the potential of this approach, a case study on dual-patient breathing during the COVID-19 outbreak has been conducted, resulting in a new type of audio data called "BreathFS," from which a transcription model has been trained.

Advanced imaging techniques like Computer Tomography (CT) scans have significantly neomedicine, yet they produce vast amounts of data that require careful analysis. While radiologists can accurately diagnose conditions, the time they save with these images could be further reduced through automated neoplasm segmentation algorithms. Despite the promise of deep learning algorithms, their application to this complex, low-contrast 3D medical imaging task has been hindered by challenges such as data imbalances and shadows cast by surrounding organs. To address these challenges, a novel deep learning architecture called DDAUnet was developed, incorporating an attention mechanism and dilated convolution to enhance performance. Through extensive testing on a comprehensive 3D CT scan dataset, DDAUnet demonstrated superior results, achieving high scores for accuracy and efficiency in comparison to existing methods.

Our proposed framework enables the creation of probabilistic models of subsurface properties, such as fluid types and rock textures, by using non-parametric methods on log data. These deterministic models are enhanced with a Bayesian inference technique to derive an assessment of the potential error margins. This results in each well test case providing an assessment of the potential error margins in our model parameters. Our showcases include the assessment of log data's impact on model parameters, a case where the data is redundant and has no impact on parameter estimates, and analysis of multiple well cases highlighting variations in uncertainty due to different matrix coefficients and the R factor. Our method leverages the ability of probabilistic models to provide realistic assessments of uncertainty upon being fed high-quality log data. This has the potential to inform well planning, well design and geosteering by offering clear insights into where and how much uncertainty exists in real-time. Our proprietary software, Ab-initio, has capabilities for well planning, well design and geosteering, but can be utilized with various deterministic models, delivering significant time and cost savings. Our proprietary Ab-initio has in-built assessment of log data's impact on model parameters, a case where the data is informative and has a narrow data range, and analysis of multiple well cases highlighting variations in uncertainty due to different matrix coefficients, geometric factors, and data quality. This method has the potential to inform well planning, well design and geosteering by offering clear insights into where and how much uncertainty exists in real-time.

Named entity recognition, an essential task in Natural Language Processing, involves detecting and categorizing meaningful real-world entities within text. The complexity of this task demands high accuracy, and the growing diversity of text on the internet has further increased its difficulty. Our research proposes a new, comprehensive approach to nested NER, treating it as a holistic text structure analysis. By leveraging a hierarchical attention mechanism and a bottom-up parsing method, our HANER model can efficiently identify nested entities at different levels of text structure, achieving state-of-the-art results on two widely used evaluation datasets without relying on pre-processed features.

We'll examine the connection between rational 2-torsion bitangents to a specific type of cubic surface and certain degenerate forms of the surface in a related mathematical space. This will enable us to perform two new actions for these bitangents on generic quartic surfaces: calculating their rational 1-cycles using a specialized method, and computing their real point counterparts with specific signs. These approaches rely on translating geometric objects into simpler, combinatorial representations. We demonstrate the application of this method to a well-known cubic surface, and for a random surface defined by a random combination of specific mathematical functions, we show the existence of 28 distinct bitangents.

This research focuses on the WSN localization problem, where the positions of non-reference nodes are determined using the known reference nodes. Traditionally, location errors are addressed with a single technology, typically based on distance or angle measurements, but this research considers WSNs with two competing measurement types - signal strength and angle - and classifies possible localization errors. It explores the impact of a common source of error, path loss exponent variability, on cross-technology measurements and analyzes how these errors influence the accuracy of TR trilateration, TW triangulation, and CTA methods. To compare the performance of these techniques, the research uses a single aperture approach to node positioning and evaluates the mean squared error (MSE) of node locations using Monte Carlo simulations, demonstrating that while the MSE of TR, TW, and CTA methods may differ with one technology involved, the MSE using two technologies is consistently lower in all cases.

Our research is centered on addressing the challenges and considerations in conducting NLP studies that examine multiple languages working in tandem. As neural networks increasingly translate text between different languages, people are starting to consume and create multilingual content that combines multiple languages. This context is increasingly relevant given that content often contains a mix of languages, whether in social media posts, product descriptions, news articles, or legal documents. To better serve this multilingual audience, we need to tackle issues related to making content understandable, searchable, and accessible through NLP across different languages. This paper delves into code-switching NLP from both theoretical and practical standpoints, offering NLP professionals guidance and a code of ethics for conducting research that respects and supports multiple languages used in conjunction.

Human-generated descriptions of images are commonly utilized to train and evaluate the performance of system-generated image descriptions. Typically, these descriptions are assessed based on their overlap with system-generated descriptions. However, this evaluation method may be flawed, as it is well established that averaging poor-performing evaluations can yield seemingly excellent results. Therefore, a key question arises: are human-generated descriptions reliable enough to be treated as independent, low-noise evaluations, or do they inherently contain significant variability that could mislead both humans and machines? In an effort to explore this issue, we conducted a study where we collected multiple diverse sets of human-generated descriptions of images that had been annotated by a large number of people. We then examined the correlation between these sets on a per-image basis and found consistently low scores. Interestingly, we also discovered that this low correlation could be attributed to two main factors: varying interpretations of color and semantic meaning, as well as the difficulty of capturing all relevant details in a short-length description. These findings shed light on the limitations of using human-generated descriptions of images to evaluate system-generated descriptions. In light of this, we propose a new method for evaluating these descriptions, which assigns scores to system-generated descriptions based on their relative performance compared to human-generated descriptions. We then demonstrated the efficacy of this method by comparing it to two widely-used alternatives and found it to be less biased and significantly more correlated with human judgments.

Our combined first-principles and Monte Carlo simulations have determined the most stable crystal structure of Ta$_2$O$_5$. In the ab initio calculations, the most stable Ta$_2$O$_5$ phase, the $\delta$-Ta$_2$O$_5$, exhibited a lattice symmetry of P1, whereas previously reported $\delta$-Ta$_2$O$_5$ structures possessed P2$_1$ symmetry. By comparing the crystallographic orientations and interatomic distances of all Ta$_2$O$_5$ structures, we established a direct correlation between the $P1$ $\delta$-Ta$_2$O$_5$ structure and earlier reports of $\alpha$-, $\gamma$-, $\delta$-, and $\sigma$-Ta$_2$O$_5$. Furthermore, our calculations indicated that Ta$_2$O$_5$ may coexist as multiple instances of the $P1$ $\delta$-Ta$_2$O$_5$ structure within a single sample, a finding with significant operational relevance to prior experimental observations.

Geographic dispersion is often cited as a potential solution to misinformation, with the assumption that a widely diverse audience reduces the spread of deceptive information. This assumption is examined in relation to Reddit's geographic configuration and its impact on the perceived credibility of fake news in the comments section. Our analysis of Reddit's geographic setup, focusing on user distribution and engagement, is carried out using data from the 2016 U.S. presidential election. It has been discovered that user accounts from the state under debate tend to receive higher engagement on both genuine and fabricated stories, with significant variations in these proportions across different states. Furthermore, our user-study results, in which participants ranked the credibility of the same set of headlines, suggest that stories shared by users from outside the state under debate are perceived as less reliable, in contrast to stories shared by in-state users which are perceived as more credible. These findings highlight that Reddit's geographic setup can significantly influence the credibility of misinformation, in accordance with the echo-chamber effect, and suggest that user diversity in terms of account origin is not a crucial factor in mitigating the echo-chamber effect.

The accelerating flow of real-time data over the internet enables modern
applications to deliver current information, yet they struggle with ensuring
accuracy. Misinformation and manipulated content, such as that produced by
deepfakes, are increasingly difficult to detect manually, especially on a large
scale. To address this challenge, we propose DDet, a neural network capable of
identifying dubious occurrences. Trained on a binary classification task, DDet
can be adapted to multi-class settings using our technique, ATT. We evaluate
DDet and ATT on a large, newly created dataset containing over a million videos
and a million audio clips. Our findings show that, with limited supervision,
DDDet and AT can achieve remarkable results in this complex environment.

The integration of speech to text converters in teaching robots how to perform tasks is currently being developed. To support this progress, the collection of a comprehensive dataset is being initiated, which will serve as a crucial resource for training effective models. The assembly of this dataset involves several stages, starting with the recruitment of human instructors who will demonstrate tasks to a helper robot using natural language. The subsequent stages include the extraction and analysis of audio data, as well as the selection of the most useful speech patterns for language models. Notably, the dataset contains a diverse range of language styles from multiple instructors, each with unique characteristics. The experiments conducted aim to evaluate various clustering techniques to group the audio data based on semantic meaning, temporal sequence, and audio features. The resulting data sets with associated labels will facilitate the advancement of effective speech recognition models.

We create an innovative framework to generate random trees with stochastic degree distributions, creating a unique approach by combining tree sequences and innovative techniques to create a broadly applicable method for creating random mixed-structure trees.

This research focuses on the sources of complexity in describing geometric field theories. A key tool utilized is a specific set of equations, known as Euler-Arnold equations, which derive from a geometric structure called a variational vector field. A particular subclass of these equations is identified and analyzed. Variational vector fields are shown to correspond to symmetries in a given equation within the Mattuck framework. It is proven that when the underlying geometry possesses a certain property (being isomorphic to a Lie group), the associated variational vector field exhibits a corresponding isomorphic relationship with a specific substructure. A new method is presented to transform an intricate mathematical object (an sigma-model) into a less complex form, specifically a structure derived from the underlying Lie group. A particular instance of this method reveals that a particular 2-dimensional field theory is, in fact, an expressive form of a fundamental mathematical concept (Euler-Arnold equation).

The proposed ABECoT is an automated evaluation framework for assessing the quality of conversational agents, comprising pre-defined tasks with goal-oriented metrics and usability metrics to determine efficiency, effectiveness, and user friendliness. 

To effectively test the capabilities of conversational agents, the framework encompasses seven key application domains: the ability to test multiple aspects of an application, 30 pre-set tasks, flexible configuration of tests, automated score calculation, visualization of results, customizable interfaces, and efficient execution management through task scheduling. 

Furthermore, ABECoT can test both goal-directed and casual conversations, providing customized scores for both implicit and explicit information, as well as user friendliness. To determine efficiency, the framework measures response times, topic control, and user training requirements, while explicit and implicit information serves as the basis for effectiveness assessment. User friendliness is determined by both emotional response and usability. 

ABECoT comprises modular components that can be utilized to test both simple and complex conversational agents, providing both specific and custom designs tests through configuration, while efficiently managing test execution. 

The framework's effectiveness and efficiency have been validated during the development of a conversational agent named iRec, a multi-domain system capable of providing personalized product recommendations, completing online forms, and controlling home appliances, via a natural language interface, through RASA. 

The framework's flexibility was demonstrated during the development of iRec, a conversational agent with multiple specialized modules that can be both customized and configured to meet

Our mathematical model identifies a small gravitational effect that would be manifested as a unique scaling pattern in the residuals of the known planets' positions, discovered by thoroughly analyzing the parameters of a dynamic model using the N-body + Newtonian approach. The detection of this effect could potentially reveal hidden characteristics of a yet-to-be-discovered Planet X within our solar system. The necessary and sufficient conditions for our method's success are highly sensitive to the specific features of Planet X, particularly its mass, which must be sufficiently substantial to be detected, but not excessively substantial, particularly in relation to its orbital distance. This criterion could be interpreted as an attempt to validate the highly eccentric and asymmetric orbital path predicted for Planet X by recent studies. The potential value of our method lies in providing an alternative mathematical framework and statistical tools for detecting the hypothetical outer planets在我们的 solar system. This, in turn, could contribute to the discovery of these celestial bodies in a manner consistent with present-day tracking of the known planets. We illustrate the potential of this approach by demonstrating that it would be possible to detect a hypothetical super-Earth located in the Sedna co-orbital region, which, although not necessarily classified as Planet X, could be added to the list of candidates in our solar system's distant scattered disc.

Recent advancements in monolingual translation memory have significantly influenced the quality of machine translation. To further investigate the potential of utilizing translation memory in the context of neural machine rendering, we have developed a rendering memory module. This module selectively utilizes translation archive to modify the disparity between rendered images and target images, thereby enhancing rendering efficiency. Our experiments conducted on MSRA-HG and ADE20K datasets have demonstrated that our proposed module can achieve significant performance gains without the need for additional trainable parameters. Notably, our rendering memory module can lead to a composite score improvement of 0.73 on the MSRA-HG dataset and the new module can achieve significant performance gains on the ADE20K dataset as well.

Researchers have analyzed the cosmic microwave background (CMB) for possible signatures of primordial black holes from the early universe, specifically within the conformal cyclic cosmology (CCC) framework. While standard models would render any such signatures indistinguishable from inflationary predictions, the CCC theory allows for observable remnants. Although initial analyses suggested the data contradicts the CCC theory due to alleged inflation-induced circles and temperature spots, these analyses used an incorrect statistical method for pattern matching. A revised analysis using a corrected algorithm reveals distinct modes of polarization in the CMB that align with CCC predictions, although they fall short of five-sigma significance. Furthermore, an updated study on temperature spots identified field-significant differences between small-scale clusters on the CMB, suggesting possible remnants of primordial black holes, in line with CCC predictions.

This study builds upon an evolving Yamabe equation framework, following the work of Kowalski-Meir and Song, which extends the classical Yamabe problem concept. The researchers have developed a stronger convergence criterion for the Yamabe evolution equation, replicating the achievements of Monticelli and Dalmasso for the standard Yamabe flow. The new approach utilizes the established energy law and a specific identity to achieve this improved convergence result.

To rapidly adapt to new tasks without retraining, the concept of few-shot learning allows models to learn from limited samples and generalize effectively. While most research has focused on few-shot classification, a significant area remains unexplored: inter-class relationships. This research proposes an innovative approach to inter-class few-shot learning, enabling the model to generalize well to entirely new categories within the same target domain, using only a small number of labeled images. The model combines a dual-branch network with a large-scale representation space and an attention-based attention bank to emphasize crucial features, then compares this with two alternative approaches on the PASCAL VOC 2007 dataset, demonstrating its superiority to both random initialization and traditional classification models with larger datasets. Significantly, it outperforms the alternative low-shot models by a significant margin, achieving a 10% margin of improvement.

To enhance cross-domain recommendation, this study focuses on two critical elements: the diverse preferences of users in multiple sparse domains and the relationship between those domains. To address these, a new approach called Multi-Sparse-Domain Cooperative Recommendation (MSDCR) is devised, which involves expanding a single-domain preference model to encompass the preferences of users across various sparse domains, assuming that similar users exhibit analogous preferences even when their activity occurs in different domains. Additionally, a connective preference learning mechanism is introduced, allowing information from one domain to aid another, enabling the transfer of both explicit and implicit knowledge between unrelated domains through the expansion of a single-domain preference matrix. Experimental results confirm that MSDCR outperforms existing methods in accuracy and efficiency.

Organic molecules form the subject of extensive scientific investigation in chemistry and physics, yet a full comprehension remains elusive due to the vast number of possible organic structures, estimated in the order of 1060. This research presents an innovative approach, Hypatia, to efficiently describe molecular and crystalline structures using H\"acker normal forms, minimizing the search space by at least 14 orders of magnitude. Hypatia integrates H\"acker forms into a comprehensive framework, enabling the seamless combination of multiple molecular structures or crystal lattices. The system is constructed using the H-normalization library and leverages H\"acker's methodologies, alongside homeomorphic distance measures, to effectively compare and identify equivalent structures. We showcase Hypatia's capabilities in comparing molecular structures, distinguishing between similar crystal forms, and detecting symmetries in both molecules and crystals. Furthermore, Hypatia facilitates a smooth integration with existing tools and libraries, facilitating the reliable exploration of material and molecular structures.

Using advanced technologies like artificial ventilation and echocardiography, combined with magnetic resonance imaging, allows for non-invasive monitoring of pregnant women, thereby reducing technical procedures that could induce complications. Specifically, AI ventilation utilizes air bubbles to improve the quality of MRI scans, though their effectiveness depends on appropriate frequency selection for each patient. These air bubbles can also mask critical areas of the fetus, making it challenging to avoid unnecessary procedures that could lead to complications. To address this, researchers are training deep learning models to evaluate MRI scan quality and predict their suitability for diagnosis. However, these models often struggle to generalize to new, unseen data. This study investigates the reasons behind this problem's complexity across multiple dimensions and provides a comprehensive framework for analyzing it. It is discovered that issues with data distribution and technical inconsistencies play a significant role in this challenge. The study also examines the impact of these factors on each dimension and their interplay on model performance. Poor classification results are primarily caused by inconsistent features affected by these factors. Moreover, the study demonstrates that a model with strong generalization capabilities can be developed by focusing on aspects related to data and technical inconsistencies. It achieves this through a combination of techniques, including balanced sample weighting, region-of-interest analysis, and attention mechanisms. The model's success is measured using a dataset of fetal scans with echocardiography, and it outperforms previous methods in terms of accurate classification.

Urban areas face significant challenges due to traffic congestion and environmental pollution caused by conventional privately owned vehicles. Electric vehicles, in turn, pose the risk of creating traffic bottlenecks and environmental pollution through their charging processes. Implementing electric vehicles requires a balanced approach to charging to minimize their adverse effects. This study focuses on enhancing the resilience of distribution networks in the face of natural disasters by integrating electric vehicles into the grid. We model an outage as an uncertainty in supply availability and treat EV arrival times and departure times as random variables. To address this problem of stochastic nature, we use a method agent-based optimization. This method represents each vehicle as an independent decision-maker with a utility function that reflects their individual interests. It also allows for charging flexibility, where the vehicles can adjust their charging processes to avoid peak times and maximize access to the grid during outages. We test the proposed method on a test feeder and demonstrate its effectiveness through simulations of EV behavior during outage events, finding that outages can actually benefit the community by allowing the grid to prioritize areas with greater need.

In cloud-based machine learning workflows and big data caching protocols, persistent memory devices are utilized to enhance storage efficiency and reduce costs. To better understand the capabilities of these devices, our research measures their performance in various scenarios, including random and sequential data access, as well as data eviction and flushing. Our results reveal that the Optane DC Module excels in sequential reads but lags in random operations, evictions, and flushing, in part due to its storage controller's limited visibility into the device's internal operations. Furthermore, the Optane DC Module's performance is significantly inferior to that of SSDs in random I/O, evictions, and flushing, which may have implications for its effectiveness in certain machine learning and caching applications.

Advanced driving assistance systems and self-driving technologies have swiftly progressed over recent years, yet their高昂 prices still hinder widespread adoption. To reduce the expense of autonomous vehicles and ensure the smooth flow of traffic, this project investigates a cooperative navigation approach that enables several manually driven cars to automatically find and reach a common destination through mutual coordination. The core of this approach lies in agents making decisions based on recurring interactions and a reward mechanism that incentivizes leading the way to the goal, which can be experimentally validated using a real car and a synchronized video recording.

This paper examines the structural, electronic, and magnetic properties of GdSn3, CmSn3, and the series GdxCm1-xSn3 (x = 0.25, 0.5, 0.75) using a full-potential linearized augmented plane wave method within a density functional theory framework. We analyze the chemical bonding, density of states, and spin-polarized magnetization for these materials, finding that they crystallize in the A7 structure and follow a derivate As4 unit cell arrangement. Our results suggest that CmSn3 is marginally unstable compared to GdSn3. Additionally, GdSn3 and the GdxCm1-xSn3 series exhibit antiferromagnetic order, whereas CmSn3 is stable in a paramagnetic state. We also investigate the effect of varying the Gd to Cm ratio (x = 0.25, 0.5, 0.75) and find that these alloys can mimic the desired characteristics of both parent compounds, offering a potential solution to produce materials with improved stability and altered magnetic behavior.

According to the Standard Model of particle physics and the Big Bang theory, certain components are missing from our understanding of visible matter in the universe. These include specific types of particles, such as baryons and mesons, which should contribute to the total matter content. However, calculations based on these foundational theories significantly exceed the observed value of the universe's matter density. Consequently, they imply that a substantial portion of visible matter remains unaccounted for. Consequently, this situation leads to an intriguing and somewhat unsettling conclusion - there could be hidden particles, such as extra, unseen mesons, bouncing unpredictably throughout our solar system

We provide a partial isometry 'a' within a finite-dimensional B-type affine finite dimensional Hopf algebra 'H', such that the algebraic structure formed by the set of elements '{}^a'a' becomes isomorphic to 'H' as a Hopf algebra. This finding generalizes a discovery previously made for finite-dimensional regular affine finite dimensional Hopf algebras.

Utilizing an external gravitational lens, we demonstrate how sub-Darc parallax corrections can enhance the distance measurements of Type Ia Supernovae, allowing us to estimate the scale of these corrections based on Hubble diagram residuals. Analyzing the Pantheon dataset of 1058 Type Ia Supernovae, we calculate the expected parallax distribution assuming a $\Lambda$CDM model and find a corresponding estimate of $A\sim 12\%$. This implies that future surveys like LSST, with enhanced precision, could potentially detect the effects of parallax. Additionally, we discuss the significance of parallax in the context of super-novae data fitting, dark energy models, and cosmological parameters.
These are the written contributions to the introduction to stochastic partial differential equations conference, held at University of Cambridge in June 2019.

In traditional metal interconnect systems, a critical threshold is reached when signal delay equals reflection, after which it becomes economically advantageous to include more memory elements. However, in photonic silicon materials, an optimal configuration emerges between these two conditions, where the delay equals reflection but includes an additional factor of one-third, corresponding to a transition point in interconnect pricing. This specific condition implies a need for a higher ratio of memory to signal components - specifically, a ratio of three to one, which could be a limiting factor in photonic integrated circuits. To address this memory requirement, this research introduces a set of innovative, highly reflective ring resonators and demonstrates their ability to meet the stringent reflection thresholds, with some designs achieving a ratio of 90 dB, but risking a increase in signal delay.

A Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) system is a medical imaging technology that utilizes Magnetic Resonance to create detailed images of the body's internal structures, including identifying tumors. However, accurately diagnosing tumors from an MRI scan can bechallenging for human radiologists, a task that is further complicated by the vast amount of data produced by these images. This difficulty is even greater when radiologists are tasked with assessing the grade of a tumor based on an fMRI scan. In this context, radiologists frequently refer to support systems like Deep Learning-based image detection systems that can pinpoint tumors or areas of concern within an MRI scan. Unfortunately, these systems are vulnerable to manipulation methods such as Generative Adversarial Networks, Simple Class Activation Mapping, and Full-Band Pass filters, which intend to deceive the support system and make it appear as though the scan is clear of tumors or clearly tumor-filled. Ultimately, radiologists would be misled into making inaccurate decisions based on the compromised information.

The classical approach to calculating Bernoulli numbers involves utilizing the generating function associated with them. Our novel method achieves degeneration of the p-adic values of the Bernoulli numbers by employing an algebraic technique, which also reveals relationships with multiple zeta values. This method can be further applied to obtain algebraic derivations of more complex structures like Multiple Zeta Values and, potentially, 'continuous' variants of these structures as well.

The observation line list used in the solar tachograph is inappropriate for research into solar differential rotation as its elements vary in sensitivity to solar activity across different activity regions and wavelengths, which negatively impacts the quality of the resulting rotational profiles. To enhance the quality of these profiles, new line lists with different characteristics are being tested to identify the best line list for retrieving rotational profiles through least-squares deconvolution. The study proposes and analyzes several line selection criteria, including methods used to choose line lists for previous studies on differential rotation, as well as the line lists employed in the solar tachograph, to evaluate their effectiveness on the quality of the retrieved rotational profiles. The research demonstrates that randomly selected line lists, particularly those spanning a wide range of formation depths and temperatures, significantly improve the quality of the resulting rotational profiles. The results show very close agreements with independent measurements, including those from spectropolarimetric observations and optically thin diagnostics, using line lists with randomly selected elements. The quality improvements achieved with the randomly selected line lists are also at least ten times greater than those possible with the line lists used in the solar tachograph and through the traditional practice of selecting only closely related atomic transitions. The study concludes that the optimal line list for applying LSDeconv should consist of several hundred atoms forming line lists over a broad range of formation depths and temperatures, including the UV range, while taking into consideration the availability of suitable observation line lists adapted for automated systems.

This research proposes an intelligent protocol called HIGP to regulate data collection in wireless sensor networks, utilizing a method that divides networks into integrity-checkable groups based on hierarchical ranges of operation. By checking the integrity of these groups, HIGP can efficiently verify the integrity of the entire network, reducing overhead checks to a single request. The algorithm dynamically selects the checking group using a formula that considers sensor energy levels and data collection demands, ensuring optimal integrity verification while minimizing checks. Experimental results demonstrate that using HIGP leads to significant improvements in checking time and maintains balance in checking loads across the network.
